body:
Spec: .adlc/specs/manifest-key-hermeticity.md, Layer 3 — read the WHOLE spec section before building; it is normative, and every clause exists because a specific attack was found without it. Design principle P2: a signing operation in a signing-required store never succeeds without a key that provably authenticates the existing ledger; refusal happens BEFORE any write.

Problem: packages/tickets/lib/evidence.mjs writes lifecycle evidence UNSIGNED, silently, when no key is present (`if (key) entry.sig = sign(...)`), and NO writer checks the key is CORRECT — a stale/wrong-repo key signs an entry that reports success locally and is rejected later by CI. Both are the delayed-CI-failure shape.

Build, per the spec's Layer 3 contracts (summarized; the spec is normative):
1. ADOPTION RECORD: `.adlc/config.json` gains `"signing": {"keyFingerprint": "<sha256(utf8 key bytes)>"}`. PRESENCE of the record IS required-mode — no mutable boolean. Ledger contents are never consulted for policy.
2. KEY CEREMONY: an adlc subcommand GENERATES the key (CSPRNG, 32 random bytes hex — 64 chars) and NEVER writes it to stdout/stderr/logs (the repo has had a key-in-transcript incident; see scripts/block-secret-exposure.mjs header): handoff is a mode-0600 file at an operator-chosen path OUTSIDE the repo (path printed, contents never); custody checkpoint = operator re-entry with terminal echo off BEFORE any descriptor swap; then the fingerprint is written. Add an output-capture leakage test asserting the key bytes never appear on any ceremony stream. Caller-supplied keys refused on the normal path; legacy import only behind an explicit audited exception flag that doctor reports.
3. WRITER CONTRACT (shared helper used by evidence writer, record.mjs, record-cross-model), when the record is present, all inside ONE manifest-lock critical section that also covers the config read for EVERY writer including the keyless legacy path: key null → refuse (error names the variable and the hardened loaders; NEVER instructs shell-sourcing a repo file); sha256(key) != fingerprint → refuse naming wrong-key and the rotation path; fingerprint match → full required-mode forest verification, any failure → refuse; only then append. No --allow-unsigned when the record is present (hard error).
4. VERIFIER CONTRACT: gate-manifest verify, tier-check, and ticket doctor apply required-mode when the record is present: unsigned/invalid/gap entries FAIL, unsigned suffix after signed history FAILS, missing/orphaned/truncated segments FAIL, wrong verifier key FAILS naming wrong-key, malformed record FAILS. Direct-tamper tests run against verifiers with no writer involved.
5. ANTI-ROLLBACK: extend the append-only-vs-base pattern (precedent: scripts preflight gate guard-findings-ledger-append-only, ADR 0014) to the manifest forest: base ledger (root + every segment) must be an exact prefix of the candidate. ONE sanctioned non-extension: a key-rotating transition passing the two-arm gate — (arm 1) candidate extends base, OR (arm 2) fingerprint CHANGED + sha256(current CI secret) matches the NEW fingerprint + full candidate verifies under the new key + candidate equals base entry-for-entry under the RECURSIVE SEMANTIC PROJECTION defined in the spec (normative; build from the spec text, not this summary): defined by exclusion not enumeration — every field not named as derived is preserved AND compared, unknown/future top-level fields included; the derived excluded set is exactly {sig, sigVersion, prev, anchor.lineHash}; anchor.segment/anchor.seq and all other anchor fields ARE compared so topology survives rotation; only an optional NEW signed suffix may follow the projected base sequence. sigVersion is excluded from payload comparison but constrained monotonically: rebuilt entries are always v2, a v1-where-base-was-v2 candidate FAILS, and a malicious-downgrade fixture is a required negative test. Integrity of rebuilt prev/anchor.lineHash comes from the independent full verification of the candidate. Required tests: anchored multi-segment rotation (positive), anchor redirection, unknown-field mutation, topology change, truncation (negative).
6. TRANSITIONS: immutable forest generations; a single atomically-replaced descriptor (the adoption record) names the active generation; every reader/writer recovers a pending transaction marker under the lock before observing state; the transition lock is stable, generation-independent, and stale-owner-reclaimable (pid+liveness+bounded takeover or OS-backed) — proven by OUT-OF-PROCESS SIGKILL tests at every commit point (a fresh process reclaims, recovers, proceeds; two live owners impossible; finally-based fault injection does not satisfy this); rotation = validate old generation under old key → generate new key + custody checkpoint → build + fully verify new generation off-path → marker → swap. INITIAL ADOPTION is a distinct transition (no old key): legacy structural validation (chain hashes intact, no gaps/orphans; absent sigs permitted HERE only) + explicit --attest-unsigned authorization + generated key + build fully-signed generation + verify + swap. Secret cutover is a serialized maintenance window: PR green on all else → admin updates secrets.ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY → gate re-run → merge immediately; rollback = restore old secret (nothing on main referenced the new key). Dual-secret grace is deliberately NOT built.
7. ANTI-ROLLBACK WIRING: the append-only-vs-base manifest-forest guard runs in BOTH CI and local preflight (scripts/preflight.mjs has a hard-coded gate list — add the gate there; precedent: guard-findings-ledger-append-only). A gate-bite test proves the same coherent rollback fails locally and in CI.
8. ROTATION AND EXTERNAL OBSERVATIONS: a fingerprint is a hash, not a key — retired-signature verification needs the retired KEYS. The adoption record carries priorFingerprints (append-only, never shrinks; dropping/reordering fails the gate) as the tree-side commitment; CI retains a KEYRING in ONE versioned secret payload — secrets.ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY becomes a newline-joined ordered list, FIRST entry current, bare single key = keyring of one (existing deployments unchanged); NO companion secret exists, so rotation rollback is one atomic secret restore; cross-checked against the tree (sha256(first)==keyFingerprint; each retired key hash matches its priorFingerprints entry in order); test K1->K2->K3 rotation plus rollback via one atomic secret update; store entries verify under the keyring member current at observation time (generation recorded at mirror time); new writes sign under the current key only; the store is never rebuilt; the rotation custody checkpoint covers retiring the old key INTO the keyring. End-to-end test: nonempty K1 store survives K2 rotation, every observed entry verifiable via the keyring, mirror step green.
9. DIRECT-CONSUMER INVENTORY (mandatory before building the descriptor): direct manifest reads/writes/lock paths/revision-ignore lists are hard-coded across model-router, ticket-sync, runner, fleet, and build-gate. Inventory every one, route all of them through ONE shared descriptor-aware resolver in the same leaf layer as the validation helper (gate-manifest -> core -> tickets is the existing graph; a resolver above tickets is unreachable from tickets without a cycle), and add regression tests per consumer package: after adoption none reads stale legacy history, misses new evidence, or folds active-generation artifacts into a revision identity.
10. OBSERVATION IDENTITY: truncation enforcement and mirror dedup identify observed entries by the recursive semantic projection (NOT by sig — re-signing at rotation replaces every signature, so a sig-keyed identity reports every prior observation missing or silently reopens truncation); pre-scheme store lines infer generation by keyring order, inference recorded on first successful verification; the keyring is ONE versioned secret payload (newline-joined; first = current, then retired keys IN priorFingerprints ORDER — one canonical chronological order shared by both lists; bare key = keyring of one; ONE parser owns the format and every fingerprint check hashes the PARSED CURRENT KEY, never the raw payload) so rollback stays one-step; observation entries record the MATCHED fingerprint explicitly at mirror time, pre-scheme lines resolve by trying every member (order-independent) with the match recorded on first verification; gate tests cover legacy single-key payload, multiline keyring, and K1->K2->K3 double rotation with observations under every generation; add the mirror+tier-check truncation-across-rotation e2e.
11. TRACKING CONTRACT: the root .gitignore blanket-ignores .adlc/* (verified: git check-ignore matches .adlc/manifest-generations/**), so add !.adlc/manifest-generations/ (and descendants) to the root .gitignore AND to every init/scaffold/migration emitter that writes gitignore rules; test: adopt, rotate, stage normally, assert the committed tree contains the complete active generation.
12. REVISION IDENTITY: all active-generation manifest artifacts (.adlc/manifest-generations/<id>/** per the descriptor) are excluded from the change-set revision digest and untracked-file refusals exactly as .adlc/manifest.jsonl is today; the adoption record itself stays review-bound. Round-trip test: record-cross-model then tier-check agree on the revision after adoption AND after rotation.
13. THIS REPO'S BOOTSTRAP — two ordered PRs, checker first: PR-A adds the gate-workflow checks (sha256(secret)-vs-tree-fingerprint comparison, required-mode assertion i.e. this repository must carry an adoption record, manifest-forest append-only guard) — all inert or trivially satisfied while no record exists on main. PR-B, judged by PR-A logic running from base, runs the initial-adoption ceremony with a FRESHLY GENERATED key (deliberate rotation away from the incumbent key, which has floated in interactive shells; see scripts/block-secret-exposure.mjs header for the incident) and the admin updates the CI secret + operator shells. doctor gains: signed entries present but no adoption record → WARN recommending adoption.

Acceptance criteria (spec AC3.1–AC3.4):
1. `node --test packages/gate-manifest/test/required-mode-writers.test.mjs` — one named case per writer row of the spec's Layer 3 matrix, each asserting written-vs-refused AND the subsequent gate-manifest verify outcome.
2. `node --test packages/gate-manifest/test/required-mode-tamper.test.mjs` — hand-tampered fixtures (stripped sigs, unsigned suffix, deleted segment, coherent rollback, record removal, wrong verifier key) each fail with the specified error class, no writer involved.
3. `node --test packages/gate-manifest/test/transitions.test.mjs` — ceremony refuses caller-supplied keys; custody checkpoint precedes swap; interruption at each commit point recovers to old-or-complete-new generation; truncation-replay of a rotation fails the semantic projection; adoption over invalid legacy history refused.
4. Refusal is side-effect-free across compound commands (spec AC3.5): node --test packages/tickets/test/lifecycle-atomicity.test.mjs — in an adopted store, ticket complete --write and ticket update --authorize --write under EACH refusal cause (missing key; wrong key; unsigned suffix in the forest; truncated segment) exit non-zero AND leave ticket shards, transaction journal, and manifest byte-identical; the manifest-policy preflight runs BEFORE the first store mutation under a lock held through the evidence append.
5. Bootstrap verified live: PR-A checks green while inert; after PR-B, `adlc ticket complete --write` on a scratch ticket produces evidence CI verifies green; a follow-up PR deleting the adoption record fails the required-mode assertion. Full suite + preflight green throughout.

Depends on the explicit-key library boundary ticket (validated required `key` param) being merged first.
title: Signing adoption: fingerprint record, fail-closed writers, required-mode verifiers, generation-switched transitions, and this repo's two-PR bootstrap
